1.semEn: one; the starting point of order
1.tipEn: As a stroke it is called 横 (the horizontal). No variants.

7.tipEn: No variants. The top stroke is shorter than the bottom one.

9.semEn: person; people; doer of an action
9.tipEn: On the left it becomes 亻 (the person radical); as a top component it appears as 𠆢, as in 今 and 合.

10.tipEn: Usually sits at the bottom, like two legs holding up the top part.

12.tipEn: As a top component it often flips into 丷, as in 关 and 曾.

18.tipEn: On the right it is written 刂; on the left or top it stays 刀, as in 分 and 切.

19.tipEn: No variants; often signals action or effort.

20.tipEn: Only appears as a top component, wrapping down to the right.

24.tipEn: No variants; it forms the skeleton of many characters.

27.tipEn: Only as a top component, covering the upper left. Originally a cliff; today often about buildings.

30.tipEn: No variants. Note: standalone 口 differs from the enclosure 囗.

31.tipEn: A fully closed box: write the inside first, then seal the frame.

32.tipEn: As a left component, the bottom horizontal becomes a rising stroke.

37.tipEn: As a top component, the right-falling stroke often becomes a dot, as in 奇.

38.tipEn: As a left component, the horizontal becomes a rising stroke and does not cross through.

39.tipEn: As a left component, the horizontal becomes a rising stroke, as in 孩.

40.tipEn: Like 冖 but with an extra dot on top; signals buildings and home.

41.tipEn: Usually bottom-right; relates to hand or measurement, as in 对, 夺, 封.

42.tipEn: As a top component it often flips into ⺌, as in 尖 and 当.

46.tipEn: As a left component, the last vertical becomes a rising stroke, as in 岭.

47.tipEn: Usually written 川 today; the curvy 巛 is very rare.

50.tipEn: Usually on the left or right (布, 帽); signals cloth products.

53.tipEn: A 厂 with a dot on top; signals buildings and places.

57.tipEn: No variants; the bow meaning extends to 'bent' or 'to draw (a bow)'.

60.tipEn: The two 撇 do NOT mean 'two'; it relates to roads and walking.

61.tipEn: On the left it becomes 忄; at the bottom it stays 心; rarely ⺗, as in 恭.

62.tipEn: Usually on the right (找, 战, 划); signals weapons and war.

63.tipEn: Traditional 戶/戸, simplified 户; signals doors and families.

64.tipEn: On the left it becomes 扌; as a top component it can appear as 龵, as in 看 and 拳.

66.semEn: to tap; to make someone do
66.tipEn: As a right component it is written 攵; originally 'to tap lightly', extends to causing actions.

67.tipEn: Looks similar to 攵 — watch the stroke shapes carefully.

69.tipEn: Usually on the right (新, 近, 听); relates to axes and cutting.

70.tipEn: Narrows as a left component (放, 旅, 族).

72.tipEn: No variants; signals the sun, time, and dates.

74.tipEn: The 'flesh 月' (脸, 肚, 脑 — body parts) looks identical to the moon's 月; tell them apart by meaning.

75.tipEn: As a left component, the right-falling stroke becomes a dot, as in 村 and 树.

76.tipEn: Usually on the right (欢, 歌, 吹); relates to the mouth exhaling.

77.tipEn: Usually left or top; as a left component, the last horizontal becomes a rising stroke, as in 此.

85.tipEn: On the left it becomes 氵 (three-dots water); at the bottom it can appear as 氺, as in 泰 and 浆.

86.tipEn: Narrows on the left as 火; at the bottom it becomes the four dots 灬, as in 热, 点, 照.

88.tipEn: Usually a top or bottom component (爸, 爷, 斧); relates to elders or weapons.

93.tipEn: As a left component the vertical becomes a rising stroke that doesn't poke through (牜); as a top component ⺧, as in 告.

94.tipEn: On the left it becomes 犭; standalone it is 犬. Both mean dogs and animals.

96.tipEn: Modern dictionaries call it the 王 radical ('jade on a slant'); as a left component the last horizontal becomes a rising stroke, as in 班 and 球.

102.tipEn: Usually a component on the left or in the middle (男, 界, 备); signals fields.

104.tipEn: Only as a top component (病, 疼, 瘦); shaped like a person leaning on a bed.

106.tipEn: No variants; 的 (built from it) is one of the most frequent characters in modern Chinese.

108.tipEn: Only at the bottom (盘, 盒, 盆); signals dishes and containers.

109.tipEn: Narrows as a left component (眠, 睛); standalone, its long horizontal is wide.

112.tipEn: Usually on the left (破, 码, 硬); signals stones.

113.tipEn: On the left it becomes 礻; at the bottom it stays 示, as in 票 and 奈.

115.tipEn: As a left component, the right-falling stroke becomes a dot, as in 和 and 种.

116.tipEn: A 宀 with 八 underneath; only as a top component; signals holes and caves.

117.tipEn: No variants; as a top component the horizontal stretches wide, as in 亲 and 帝.

118.tipEn: Only as a top component, written ⺮ — like two 个 shapes side by side.

119.tipEn: As a left component, the right-falling stroke becomes a dot (粉, 糖, 粗).

120.tipEn: On the left it becomes 纟; at the bottom it stays 糸, as in 素 and 紧.

123.tipEn: As a left component or top, the last vertical becomes a 撇 and horizontals become rising strokes (样, 着).

128.tipEn: Usually on the left (听, 取) or inside an enclosure (闻).

133.tipEn: No variants; appears as a component (到, 室, 致).

135.tipEn: Usually on the left (话, 活, 刮); signals tongue and speech.

137.tipEn: As a left component, the last horizontal becomes a dot and doesn't poke through (船, 航).

140.tipEn: Listed as 艸 in dictionaries but written 艹 (花, 草, 茶); only as a top component; signals plants.

142.tipEn: Usually left or right (虾, 蚊, 蛋); signals insects and creepy-crawlies.

144.tipEn: Its two halves wrap around the middle (街, 衡, 衔); signals roads and walking.

145.tipEn: On the left it becomes 衤 (裙, 袜); at the bottom it stays 衣 (装, 裂).

147.tipEn: Traditional 見, simplified 见; usually right or bottom (现, 觉, 视).

149.tipEn: On the left it becomes 讠 (说, 话, 请); elsewhere it stays 言 (信, 警).

154.tipEn: Traditional 貝, simplified 贝; signals money and trade (贵, 购, 贸).

156.tipEn: Usually a bottom-left wrapper (起, 超, 赶); a 土 with an extra short 撇 on top.

157.tipEn: On the left it becomes ⻊ with the last stroke as a rising stroke (跑, 路, 踢).

158.tipEn: As a left component, the last horizontal becomes a rising stroke without poking through (躺, 躲); sits on the right in 射.

159.tipEn: Traditional 車, simplified 车; narrows on the left (转, 轮).

162.tipEn: Written 辶 (the 'walking' wrap); only as a bottom-left wrapper (过, 送, 远); signals walking.

163.tipEn: On the right it becomes 阝 (the right-ear radical: 都, 那, 郊); signals cities and places. Don't confuse it with the left-ear 阜.

164.tipEn: Usually on the left (酒, 配, 醉); shaped like a wine jar.

167.tipEn: On the left it becomes 钅 (钱, 银, 铁); at the bottom or right it stays 金 (鑫, 鉴).

169.tipEn: Traditional 門, simplified 门; forms an outer frame (间, 问, 闪); signals doors and gates.

170.tipEn: On the left it becomes 阝 (the left-ear radical: 队, 防, 阶); signals hills and mounds. Don't confuse it with the right-ear 邑.

173.tipEn: Only as a top component (雪, 雷, 霜); signals weather.

174.tipEn: Traditional 靑, simplified 青; a component in 清, 情, 晴; signals color.

177.tipEn: Usually on the left (鞋, 鞭, 鞍); signals leather goods.

180.tipEn: Usually at the bottom or right (暗, 意, 韵); signals sound.

181.tipEn: Traditional 頁, simplified 页; usually on the right (顶, 颜, 题); signals head and face.

182.tipEn: Traditional 風, simplified 风; usually an outer frame or on the right (飘, 枫, 疯).

184.tipEn: On the left it becomes 饣 (饭, 饿, 饱); standalone or at the bottom it stays 食 (餐).

187.tipEn: Traditional 馬, simplified 马; narrows on the left (骑, 驶, 验).

194.tipEn: Usually a component (魂, 魄, 魔); signals ghosts and the strange.

195.tipEn: Traditional 魚, simplified 鱼; narrows on the left (鲜, 渔, 鲸).

196.tipEn: Traditional 鳥, simplified 鸟; on the left or right (鸡, 鸭, 鹅).

199.tipEn: Traditional 麥, simplified 麦; seen in 麦/麸; the 'flour' character is 麵 in traditional script.

201.tipEn: Traditional 黃, simplified 黄; seen in 黄/簧/磺.

210.tipEn: Traditional 齊, simplified 齐; seen in 齐/剂/挤.

211.tipEn: Traditional 齒, simplified 齿; seen in 齿/龄/啮; signals teeth and age.

212.tipEn: Traditional 龍, simplified 龙; seen in 龙/笼/聋.

2.semEn: a vertical line; to run through
2.tipEn: As a stroke it is called 竖 (the vertical); usually on a character's central axis.

3.tipEn: As a stroke it is called 点 (the dot); usually on top or at the upper right.

4.tipEn: As a stroke it is called 撇 (the left-falling stroke); drawn from upper right to lower left.

5.tipEn: As a stroke it is called 横折弯钩; has variants like 乚, 乛, ⺄.

6.tipEn: As a stroke it is called 竖钩 — a vertical ending in a left hook.

8.tipEn: Only as a top component: a dot plus a horizontal. No variants.

11.tipEn: Easily confused with 人: short 撇 + long 捺 = 入; long 撇 + short 捺 = 人.

13.tipEn: Only as an outer frame, covering the top, left, and right.

14.tipEn: Like 宀 but without the dot; also means 'to cover'.

15.tipEn: Don't confuse with 氵: 冫 = cold and frozen, 氵 = flowing water.

16.tipEn: No variants; standalone it is a small table; as a component it often relates to small objects.

17.tipEn: Usually a bottom frame (画, 凶): closed on three sides, open on top.

21.tipEn: On the left it is often written as a vertical-plus-hook shape (as in 此); originally a small spoon.

22.tipEn: A box open on the right, wrapping the parts inside.

23.tipEn: Looks like 匚 but with the left side extended; much rarer.

25.tipEn: As a component, the dot often becomes a short 撇, as in the right side of 外.

26.tipEn: Usually bottom-right; looks like an ear, hence the nickname 'single ear'.

28.tipEn: No variants; usually tucked into a corner (去, 公, 台).

29.tipEn: As a component, the right-falling stroke becomes a long dot (对, 欢); originally meant 'right hand'.

33.tipEn: Easily confused with 土: long top + short bottom = 士.

34.tipEn: Easily confused with 夊: 夂 has 3 strokes, 夊 has 4.

35.tipEn: 4 strokes; usually at the bottom (夏, 麦).

36.tipEn: No variants; distinguish from 夂: 夕 = dot + 撇 + horizontal-撇.

43.tipEn: Easily confused with 兀: 尢's 撇 has a hook; signals leg problems.

44.tipEn: The 'corpse' meaning has faded; mostly signals houses or bodies (屋, 居, 尿).

45.tipEn: Almost never standalone; usually absorbed into the grass or mountain radicals.

48.tipEn: No variants; as a component it is often stretched wide and flat.

49.tipEn: Tell apart 已/巳: open top = 己, half-open = 已, closed = 巳.

51.tipEn: No variants; a common standalone character (干净, 干部).

52.tipEn: Same origin as 纟 — both mean thread; 幺 stresses smallness.

54.tipEn: Easily confused with 辶: 廴 has 2 strokes and no dot; 辶 has 3 strokes.

55.tipEn: Usually at the bottom (开, 异, 弃); two hands lifting something up.

56.tipEn: A slanted hook plus a dot — like 戈 minus one 撇.

58.semEn: an animal snout; a hand tool
58.tipEn: Usually middle or bottom (当, 雪, 灵); the middle horizontal may or may not poke out left.

59.tipEn: Three 撇 usually on the right; signals hair, patterns, or rays of light.

65.tipEn: Usually upper-right or left (枝, 翅); signals support and branching.

68.tipEn: Usually on the left (料, 科); relates to measuring and scooping.

71.tipEn: Easily confused with 旡 (the right side of 既) — watch the top stroke.

73.tipEn: Easily confused with 日: 曰 is flat and wide; 日 is tall and narrow.

78.tipEn: A 夕 with an extra horizontal; signals death and disaster.

79.tipEn: Usually on the right (段, 设, 没); originally a weapon, extends to striking.

80.tipEn: Modern dictionaries mostly merge it into 母: 母 has two dots, 毋 has one crossbar through.

81.tipEn: No variants; originally two people side by side, extended to 'compare'.

82.tipEn: Usually left or bottom (尾, 笔, 毯); the 撇 often pokes through.

83.tipEn: No variants; signals surnames; like 氐 but without the dot.

84.tipEn: Only as a top wrapper covering the lower right; the last stroke stretches right (氛, 氧).

87.tipEn: As a top component it flips into 爫 (爱, 受, 采).

89.tipEn: Almost never standalone; only in a few characters about crossing.

90.tipEn: As a left component it is written 丬 (壮, 状, 将).

91.tipEn: The mirror image of 爿; originally a wood slice.

92.tipEn: No variants; usually on the left (鸦, 雅, 芽).

95.tipEn: No variants; seen in a few characters like 率, 畜, 玄.

97.tipEn: Usually wraps in the middle of a character (瓣, 瓢); a melon hanging on the vine.

98.tipEn: Usually on the right (瓶, 瓷); signals clay and pottery.

99.tipEn: Usually middle or bottom (甜, 甚); signals taste.

100.tipEn: No variants; signals growth and birth.

101.tipEn: Usually a component (甬, 甩, 勇); signals implements and use.

103.tipEn: Easily confused with 正; usually at the bottom (蛋, 楚).

105.tipEn: Only as a top component (登, 发); two feet walking apart.

107.tipEn: Usually on the left (波, 被, 破); signals skin and surfaces.

110.tipEn: No variants; signals spears and sharpness.

111.tipEn: As a left component, the right-falling stroke becomes a dot (短, 知).

114.tipEn: Almost never standalone; hides at the bottom of 禹, 离, 禽.

121.tipEn: Usually on the left (缸, 缺, 罐); signals jars and pottery.

122.tipEn: As a top component it is written 罒 (罗, 罚, 置); nicknamed the 'four top' but unrelated to 四.

124.tipEn: Usually on the right (翔, 翘); as a top component the two 习 stand side by side (翼).

125.tipEn: As a top component it is written 耂 (考, 者, 孝); signals old age.

126.tipEn: Usually a top or bottom component (需, 耍, 耐).

127.tipEn: Usually on the left (耕, 耗); signals farm tools and farming.

129.tipEn: As a left component the vertical becomes a 撇 (律, 肆); a hand writing with a brush.

130.tipEn: The standalone 肉 radical is rare (as in 腐); modern dictionaries mostly merge it into 月 (the 'flesh moon').

131.tipEn: No variants; as a component the vertical becomes a 撇 (the left side of 临, 卧).

132.tipEn: Originally a picture of a nose; usually a top component (息, 臭, 鼻).

134.tipEn: Usually bottom or lower-left (舀, 舅, 插); relates to pounding grain.

136.tipEn: Almost never standalone; only in 舞, 舜, etc.

138.tipEn: Usually on the right (很, 跟, 根); easily confused with 良 — check the extra dot.

139.tipEn: Usually bottom or right (绝, 艳); signals color and looks.

141.tipEn: Only as a top component (虎, 虑, 虚); signals tigers.

143.tipEn: Only a component (恤, 衅); a 撇 on top of 皿 — like a drop of blood falling.

146.tipEn: Listed as 西 in modern dictionaries; a top component (要, 票, 栗); a covering shape.

148.tipEn: Usually left or middle (解, 触, 衡); signals horns and angles.

150.tipEn: Usually a top or left component (容, 欲, 俗); 'valley' extends to 'contain'.

151.tipEn: Usually left or middle (豌, 痘, 壹); originally an ancient stemmed dish.

152.tipEn: Originally a pig; 家 is literally 'a pig under a roof' — settled living.

153.tipEn: Usually on the left (豹, 豺, 貌); signals cat-like beasts.

155.tipEn: Usually left or bottom (赦, 赫); signals red and bareness.

160.tipEn: Usually on the left (辣, 辨); signals hardship and punishment.

161.tipEn: No variants; used in 晨, 震, 辱, 唇.

165.tipEn: Easily confused with 采 (爫+木): 釆 is a 撇 over 米, 7 strokes in total.

166.tipEn: No variants; a component in 野, 量, 埋.

168.tipEn: Traditional 長, simplified 长; few simplified characters use this radical (套, 肆).

171.tipEn: No variants; seen in 隶, 逮, 康; signals catching and attachment.

172.tipEn: Usually on the right (谁, 难, 推); originally a short-tailed bird; distinct from the 鸟 radical.

175.tipEn: On the left (排, 辈) or middle (悲, 罪); two verticals turned away from each other.

176.tipEn: Rarely a component; mostly used standalone.

178.tipEn: Traditional 韋, simplified 韦; seen in 韧, 韩, 韬.

179.tipEn: Almost never standalone — it basically IS the leek character.

183.tipEn: Traditional 飛, simplified 飞; few simplified characters use this radical (飞, 飒, 飓).

186.tipEn: Usually a top component (香, 馨, 馥); grain giving off fragrance.

188.tipEn: Usually on the left (骼, 髋); signals bones.

189.tipEn: Usually a component (敲, 膏, 稿); shaped like a tall watchtower.

190.tipEn: Only as a top component (髦, 鬓, 髻); long hair flowing down.

191.tipEn: Traditional 鬥; in simplified script, characters like 闹/阅 merged into 门; rare in simplified.

192.tipEn: Only in 鬯 and 鬱 (the traditional form of 郁); a vessel of ritual wine.

193.tipEn: Originally a three-legged cooking pot; seen in 融, 鬻.

197.tipEn: Traditional 鹵, simplified 卤; signals saltiness and brine.

198.tipEn: Usually a top component (麓, 麋, 麟); a deer seen from the side.

200.tipEn: A 广 over two 木; usually a top component (麻, 磨, 糜).

202.tipEn: Originally glutinous millet; seen in 黍, 黏, 黎; signals grains and stickiness.

203.tipEn: Usually a top or left component (墨, 默, 黛); shaped like something smoked black in a chimney.

204.tipEn: Rarely used; stitching patterns like embroidery needlework.

205.tipEn: Traditional 黽, simplified 黾; characters for large turtles and crocodiles belong here.

206.tipEn: Originally a three-legged, two-eared ritual vessel; almost always used standalone.

207.tipEn: The left is 壴 (a drum stand), the right is 支 (a hand striking); almost always standalone.

208.tipEn: Usually standalone or a top component (鼠, 鼬, 鼹); a rat with open mouth and bared teeth.

209.tipEn: 自 + 畀; only as a top component (鼻, 鼾); signals noses.

213.tipEn: Traditional 龜, simplified 龟; very few simplified characters use this radical.

214.tipEn: Originally a panpipe; extremely rare, mostly in ancient texts.
